author: ETA PRIME
description:
Valve has officially raised the price of the Steam Deck OLED — and the increases are massive. The 512GB model jumped from $549 to $789, and the 1TB model went from $649 all the way up to $949. That's up to a $300 increase overnight. In this video I break down exactly what happened, why Valve made this move, and whether the Steam Deck is still worth buying at these new prices.
Valve's statement: "Steam Deck itself hasn't changed; these new prices reflect the current state of component costs and other global logistical challenges across the industry as a whole."
Both OLED models are currently back in stock. Certified refurbished models including the older LCD version are still available at lower price points starting at $319.

Today we're taking another look at the ASRock BC250 PC, but this time, things are completely different. This inexpensive server blade is actually powered by the exact same APU found inside the PlayStation 5, but out of the box, it's locked down to just 24 Compute Units.
Well, the game has changed! Thanks to an incredible community mod, we can now fully unlock all 40 CUs on the RDNA 2 GPU, bringing this thing right up to PS5 spec. In this video, I'll show you exactly how to apply the unlock in Bazzite OS, take a look at my custom 3D-printed case and cooling setup, and run some intense gaming benchmarks to see just how much free performance we're getting. From Cyberpunk 2077 to Ghost of Tsushima, the gains are absolutely wild!
